source_text:
ὁρώμενον καὶ νοούμενον, χωρητὸν καὶ ἀχώρητον, ἵν' ὅλῳ ἀνθρώπῳ τῷ αὐτῷ καὶ
Θεῷ ὅλος ἄνθρωπος ἀναπλασθῇ ὁ πεσὼν ὑπὸ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν. γʹ. Ἐπειδὴ γὰρ
ἐσαρκώθη ζωὴ κατὰ φύσιν ὑπάρχων ὁ Μονογενὴς τοῦ Θεοῦ Λόγος, ἀνέθαλλεν εἰς
ζωὴν ἡ ἀνθρώπου φύσις· γέγονε γὰρ "πρωτεύων ἐν πᾶσιν αὐτός."
thought_title: The whole human being refashioned in the one who is both God and man
orientation: Cyril continues his description of the one Christ as both visible and invisible, then states the purpose: that the whole fallen human being might be refashioned in the same one who is both God and man.
pass_a_gloss: being seen and being thought, [being] containable and [being] uncontainable, in order that in [the] whole man [who is] the same [one] also God [the] whole man might be refashioned, the [one] having fallen under the sin. 3. For since [he] was enfleshed, being life by nature, the only Son of God [the] Word, the nature of man blossomed up into life; for he has become "being first in all things himself."

choices.why: Keeps the passive participles as participles to preserve the parallel with the preceding adjectives; 'thought' renders νοούμενον as the object of intellectual perception, not mere opinion.
Preserves the root χωρέω (to make room for, contain) and the privative alpha; matches the spatial sense Cyril uses for the body versus the uncircumscribed divinity.
Glossary term; the prefix ἀνα- suggests remaking or reshaping, not creation from nothing.
Keeps φύσις as 'nature' and the genitive as possessive; avoids the banned rendering 'human nature' for σάρξ, though here φύσις is the noun.
The verb ἀναθάλλω means to sprout or bloom again; the prefix ἀνα- gives the upward or renewed sense, and εἰς ζωὴν marks the goal.

choices.english: being first in all things himself
choices.why: The participle πρωτεύων keeps the verbal force; 'himself' renders the emphatic αὐτός; the phrase echoes Colossians 1:18.

pass_b_english: He is seen and thought, containable and uncontainable, so that the whole human being who fell under sin might be refashioned in the whole human being who is the same one and God. For since the only Son, the Word of God, being life by nature, was enfleshed, the nature of man blossomed up into life. For he himself has become first in all things (Colossians 1:18).

problems.quote: For he himself is first in all things
problems.why: English omits 'γέγονε' (has become/came to be). Source says 'for he has become first in all things', not simply 'is'. The 'became' is theologically significant - humanity's nature blossomed because he BECAME first in all things through incarnation.
problems.fix: For he himself has become first in all things (Colossians 1:18).
problems.ruling: γέγονε ('has become') is omitted; English 'is' loses incarnation's transformative meaning theologically significant here.

edits.old: For he himself is first in all things (Colossians 1:18).
edits.new: For he himself has become first in all things (Colossians 1:18).

last_rejected.why: 'Blossomed up' is too weak; ἀνέθαλλεν means sprouted/grew anew, connoting revival/resurrection, not mere flowering.
last_rejected.fix: the nature of man sprouted up into life
last_rejected.ruling: ἀνέθαλλεν means sprout/grow anew; 'blossomed up' captures renewal imagery adequately within normal range
